frozen_original.title: Trump Fires 17 Inspectors General Overnight Without Congressional Notice
frozen_original.synopsis: In a late-night purge on January 20, 2025, Trump fired 17 sitting inspectors general across multiple federal agencies without providing the legally required 30-day advance notice to Congress. The IGs are independent watchdogs who investigate fraud, waste, and abuse within federal agencies and report to both the executive and legislative branches. Legal experts argued the firings violated the Inspector General Act, which was specifically designed to protect IGs from political retaliation. Congress members from both parties condemned the action as a direct assault on government accountability. The sweeping purge eliminated oversight officials who might have investigated DOGE and other Trump initiatives.

frozen_original.title: Trump Threatens to Abolish the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, after the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals — which covers California, the Pacific Northwest, Hawaii, and Alaska — issued multiple rulings blocking Trump administration immigration actions, Trump publicly threatened to push for the abolition or restructuring of the 9th Circuit, which he called a 'disgrace' and a 'rogue court.' The threat echoed similar proposals from his first term but took on new urgency given the administration's open defiance of court orders. Republican legislators in Congress introduced bills to split the 9th Circuit or add seats to dilute the influence of its existing judges. Legal scholars noted the 9th Circuit had the largest geographic jurisdiction of any circuit court and served a population of over 70 million Americans. The threats were widely understood as political intimidation aimed at chilling adverse rulings, an assault on the constitutional structure of an independent federal judiciary.
